subject: Urgent: request for redacted penetration test report and remediation timeline
messages:
From: Taylor Price <taylor.price@credifin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@credifin.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent: request for penetration test report and remediation details

Sofia —

We observed a spike of anomalous requests hitting our integration logs this morning tied to API keys provisioned for Redwood. Our security team has asked for the latest penetration test report you have, redacted as needed, plus a summary of any findings that might affect our integration (S3/object storage, token handling, auth flows). We also need the remediation timeline for any medium/critical issues.

Can you provide the redacted report and an assurance on whether the issue we flagged is covered by your last engagement? If not, please confirm when you will run a focused retest and how you’ll share evidence.

This is urgent for our incident review — copying security@credifin.com.

Thanks,
Taylor Price
Information Security — CrediFin Bank
(t) 555-0199

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Taylor Price <taylor.price@credifin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for penetration test report and remediation details

Taylor —

Thanks for the heads up and for looping security. I’ve escalated to our security lead (Marissa) and customer success (David) and we’ll get you the materials ASAP. A few quick clarifying questions to make sure we only release what's necessary:

- Can you confirm the specific integration or API key IDs you saw in the logs (if you can share the request IDs that helps match to our telemetry)?
- Do you need the full pen test report or would a redacted PDF plus remediation log satisfy your audit team? We can produce both but full unredacted reports require an NDA/attestation for most customers.
- Are you expecting SOC 2 control mappings for the findings (we can attach our mapping to CC6/CC7 controls)?

We have a November 2025 third-party pen test (engagement RW-PT-2025-11). I will ask Marissa to pull the redacted PDF and a short remediation status summary for any open items.

I’ll follow up with the attachments and a suggested 30-min call to walk through the findings.

—Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Security Lead | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com

From: Taylor Price <taylor.price@credifin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@credifin.com, procurement@credifin.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:27:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for penetration test report and remediation details

Sofia —

Thanks. We can accept a redacted PDF and a remediation log. For context: the anomalous requests showed an attempt to enumerate resource objects on 2026-05-18 03:11 UTC using what appears to be session tokens tied to an integration with CrediFin. We’re particularly concerned about any findings classified as "token handling" or "insufficient access controls" in your report.

If you could:
- Highlight whether those classes of issues were present in RW-PT-2025-11 (even redacted and summarized)
- Provide remediation dates or whether fixes were completed and validated
- Attach SOC 2 control mapping for relevant findings (CC6 / CC7 / CC8)

Procurement has asked to hold renewal activity pending the outcome; copying them so we can coordinate any required T&Cs or data handling addenda.

We appreciate the quick turnaround.

Taylor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Taylor Price <taylor.price@credifin.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for penetration test report and remediation details

Taylor —

Attaching a redacted copy of our November 2025 third-party penetration test engagement (redwood-pt-report-202511-redacted.pdf). The attachment removes tester tooling output and any customer-identifying PII; per our standard process we also redact specific exploit PoCs.

Summary of findings relevant to token handling and access controls (high/medium items only):
- RW-PT-2025-11-FIND-03 (Medium): session token leakage in a legacy logging path — remediation: removed token logging and rotated affected tokens. Fix deployed 2025-12-04; verification completed 2025-12-10 (internal validation and re-scan).
- RW-PT-2025-11-FIND-07 (High): insufficient ACL on a service-side bucket used for temporary model artifacts — remediation: ACL corrected, bucket policy hardened, automated ACL test added. Fix deployed 2025-12-15; third-party validation completed 2026-01-05.

Remediation evidence: we’ve exported the remediation ticket history and validation notes to a secure Jira item: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-PT-482 (read-only link provided). I’m also attaching a lightweight remediation log (redwood-remediation-log-credifin-jira-link.txt) with the ticket IDs and dates.

SOC 2 control mapping for the two findings above is included in the PDF appendix (mapping to CC6/CC7). If procurement needs a signed attestation for the redacted report we can route through our legal team — that typically takes 48–72 hours.

If you want, I can join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the redactions and timeline; propose 2026-05-21 10:00 AM ET.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood-pt-report-202511-redacted.pdf, redwood-remediation-log-credifin-jira-link.txt

From: Taylor Price <taylor.price@credifin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@credifin.com, security@credifin.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: request for penetration test report and remediation details

Marissa/Sofia —

Received the redacted report and remediation log — thank you for the quick response and the clear timeline. A couple follow-ups before we close our incident review:

1) Can you confirm the exact date when the affected session tokens were rotated (UTC timestamp) and whether any customer-facing API keys were part of the rotation?
2) For RW-PT-2025-11-FIND-07 (the bucket ACL), can you share the date of the third-party validation run and the validator name (redacted is fine)?
3) We’d like to take you up on the 30-min call; 2026-05-21 10:00 AM ET works for our folks — please send a calendar invite with dial-in and an access-controlled recording link.

If you can include the two timestamps in an updated remediation log (or point to the Jira item with timestamps), procurement will unblock renewal hold once we have that evidence and the call completes.

Thanks again — we’ll be on the call.

Taylor Price
Information Security — CrediFin Bank
